J1.title: FS-123, question 1: the bends, on a fragment
J1.step: (`plans/STUB-qfree-ring.md` ll. 29–31): "1. **The bends, on a fragment** (the invention signal, below). Does bending a fragment on a neighbourhood of `B̄(p, 1 + ε)` keep it in FS116-Y4-EMPTY's class and leave its ring free of every arc but the (Q) arcs? If yes, EMPTY excludes at `1 + ε` every four-colour vertex of the non-Siamese simple class whose ring carries no (Q) arc, and FS114-N7-3T's, FS114-N7-HUB's and FS114-N6-RING60's classes are empty there."

J2.title: FS-124, case 1: SEMI-PAR3
J2.step: (`plans/STUB-q-ring.md` ll. 25–29): "1. **SEMI-PAR3** (inventory items 96, 97): "in a non-Siamese simple valid fragment on a closed disc of radius above 1 about a vertex p of at least four colours, no change point of the ring is a full parallel semi-hub of exactly three colours" — GAP: "the step from the bowtie's four-colour parallel semi-hub to three colours — removing the tile of p toward y from y (kind O), or the outer tile (kind T) — is excluded by no cone at p, u, y or v; a proof must read y's own ring, which carries three absent colours and no parity". A construction by formula (FS114-Y2-BOWTIE with its tip `t2` removed from `top`) or a reason none exists decides it."

J3.title: FS-125: NO-SAT, through its cases
J3.step: (`plans/STUB-saturated-local.md` ll. 21–22): "**NO-SAT** (`data/fs116/claims.md` § 4): "there are an explicit radius `R`, one `R` for every complexity, Siamese pairs allowed, and a derivation that no valid fragment on the closed disc of radius `R` about a vertex of at least four colours is saturated on the closed disc of radius `R − 1` about it.""

That is honest saturation at six (C121-SAT6). On the cover"

J5.title: FS-124, case 4: the five- and six-colour vertices
J5.step: (`plans/STUB-q-ring.md` ll. 36–39): "4. **The five- and six-colour vertices** (item 61): a five-colour vertex's ring has no change point and (Q) arcs over at least half of it (FS116-N2-FIVERING); a six-colour vertex's ring is six 60° (Q) arcs, one per tile of `p`, with outer colours constrained (FS116-N2-SIXRING). One family dies below `√3` (FS116-Y2-SIXOFF, Siamese pairs allowed); a fragment by formula holds `B̄(p, R)` for every `R < 3/2` (FS116-Y2-SIXFRAG, exact). De Grey and Gibbs left this vertex's next layer undone in 2018 (`[Polymath16threads]` [08.17]–[08.18])."

J6.title: FS-124, case 2: the disk's corner
J6.step: (`plans/STUB-q-ring.md` ll. 30–33): "2. **The closed change point, the disk's corner** (FS116-RING-Q's GAP; items 40, 97): a change point of two colours whose `±60°` points lie inside (Q) arcs. RING-Q is false below radius `≈ 1.5985` (FS116-N1-QDISK: `[Polymath2021]` Fig. 10's disk about its corner), and any exclusion on `B̄(p, 2)` must read the far side of `p`, in the directions `(ψ + 157.4°, ψ + 324.5°)` (FS116-Y2-DCREAD). A fragment by formula beyond radius 2 holding the configuration makes RING-Q false in its class."

J7.title: FS-123 question 3 with FS-124 case 7: the Siamese and non-simple classes (one step, stated twice)
J7.step: (`plans/STUB-qfree-ring.md` ll. 35–37): "3. **The Siamese and non-simple forms of EMPTY.** C114-LOCAL-F allows Siamese pairs (tiles of one colour inside each other's exclusion annulus). FS116-V6's route used non-Siamese "only for the uniqueness of `R⁻`, `R⁺` and of the tip" and simplicity only at its last step; FS116-Y4-FLANK is colour-free with Siamese pairs allowed; FS116-N1-GERM-S is RING-GERM without non-Siamese. Does the Γ-free type die at `1 + ε` with Siamese pairs allowed, or with non-simple tiles?"
